content:
Jordan L.: FYI SCA scan flagged `civetweb` in the storage-service build image as a CVE candidate.
Aisha K.: which CVE id and which transitive path?
Jordan L.: scanner output points to CVE-2024-XXXX (possible FP). Path: storage-service -> native-archive -> civetweb (vendored in build container). Not used at runtime by our service.
Jordan L.: I'm opening this thread to request a short-lived allowlist (7 days) while we confirm FP and coordinate a backport. Proposed compensating controls below.
Priya S.: please list the mitigations. we need to be comfortable before approving any temporary exception.
Jordan L.: Mitigations:
  - civetweb only present in the build image (CI runners) not in production artifacts
  - builds run in ephemeral GKE pods with node auto-delete and no hostNetworking
  - image is scanned and signed; we will block promotion to prod images until patch verified
  - KMS-encrypted artifact signing keys rotated weekly; build key usage audited
  - temporary allowlist window: 7 days; owner: @Jordan L.; tracking ticket: RISK-452
Jordan L.: Repro steps / evidence:
```
# show vulnerable file in build image
docker run --rm my-registry/storage-build:latest bash -lc "grep -R \"civetweb\" /usr/local/lib || true"
# SCA output snippet
snyk test --json | jq '.vulnerabilities[] | select(.module=="civetweb")'
```
Aisha K.: can you paste the exact `snyk` snippet (redacted) and confirm no runtime sockets exposed?
Jordan L.: pasted below (redacted):
```
{
  "module": "civetweb",
  "id": "SNYK-JS-CIVETWEB-XXXX",
  "severity": "medium",
  "packageManager": "generic",
  "path": ["storage-service", "native-archive", "civetweb"],
  "isPipEnv": false
}
```
Jordan L.: Confirmed: CI runners do not expose host network and do not bind external ports. The vendored civetweb is only used for a small build-time helper to produce a tarball; we strip binaries from final image.
Max F.: ok - sounds plausible. A couple asks: 1) can we build an image from a patched base and validate? 2) who signs off on the risk today?
Jordan L.: 1) I built a patched base and validated local build; will push image to `staging` and run integration smoke. 2) asking Priya and Aisha for security approval + an eng owner (Aisha?) to accept service-level risk.
Priya S.: Required for approval: link to staging image, confirmation of non-prod exposure, expiration date, and mitigation steps documented in RISK-452. Also want CI job that fails on any runtime inclusion.
Jordan L.: ack. staging image: `gcr/redwood/storage-build:staging-civetweb-patch-2024-11-03`. CI job added: `ci/check-no-vendor-runtime.sh` (will fail if civetweb present in final artifact). I'll attach the job in RISK-452.
risk-bot: Risk acceptance request created: RISK-452 by Jordan L. (expires in 7 days) — approvers: Priya S., Aisha K.
Aisha K.: Approved pending confirmation that the CI check is green and the staging image is scanned. Please link the scan results here.
Jordan L.: CI check passed locally; pushed staging image and ran scanner. Scan report: `https://scans.internal/reports/RISK-452-scan.html` (access internal). Results show no runtime inclusion and only build-time reference.
Priya S.: reviewed scan, CI job, and compensating controls. Approving temporary allowlist for 7 days. Please escalate to sec-review if vendor releases a patch earlier.
Aisha K.: +1 from eng side. we will prioritize backport in the next sprint.
Jordan L.: thanks all. I'll mark RISK-452 approved and close the exception after verification or earlier if upstream patch drops. :thumbsup:
Priya S.: note: log this approval in the risk register and add reminder to rotate signing key after closure."
